deck: This week, geopolitical tensions and market movements shape the aerospace landscape.

stories.head: Russia's GPS Jamming Hits New Heights
stories.body: Russia has ramped up its GPS jamming efforts, particularly over the Eastern Mediterranean, returning to pre-2024 levels. This new wave of interference raises concerns for U.S. navigation systems and could complicate military operations in the region. With global tensions simmering, the implications for defense procurement are clear: expect a surge in demand for more resilient navigation technologies.
stories.soWhat: If you're betting on GPS alternatives, now might be the time to double down.

stories.head: Quantum Space to Go Public via SPAC
stories.body: Quantum Space is set to go public through a SPAC merger, which may raise eyebrows given the recent SPAC fatigue in the market. The deal is expected to value the company at around $1 billion, showcasing that even in a cooling market, some firms believe they can still ride the wave of investor interest. This move could signal a renewed appetite for space tech among public investors.
stories.soWhat: If SPACs are back on the menu, expect more aerospace startups to dust off their prospectuses.

stories.head: True Anomaly Secures $190M Series C
stories.body: True Anomaly has raised $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This round underscores a robust interest in co-orbital security and space domain awareness technologies, particularly as DoD contracts become more lucrative. The funding will fuel further development in a sector that's increasingly seen as critical to national security.
stories.soWhat: In a world of rising threats, co-orbital security is not just a niche; it’s becoming a necessity.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on GPS alternatives
watchlist.body: With jamming intensifying, companies focused on resilient navigation solutions could see increased interest.

watchlist.title: SPAC deals may surge again
watchlist.body: As Quantum Space's public listing unfolds, other startups might follow suit, reigniting the SPAC conversation.

watchlist.title: Funding rounds could accelerate
watchlist.body: With True Anomaly's success, expect other space firms to seek funding as defense budgets expand.

watchlist.title: Watch for more co-orbital activity
watchlist.body: As tensions rise, we may see increased investments in technologies aimed at countering threats in space.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
